title: Churches that don't file are invisible
bullets: §6033(a)(3)(A)(i) exempts churches from filing Form 990.
The 15,656 church-status filers here are a self-selecting subset: ECFA members, federal-grant recipients under the Single Audit Act, religious nonprofits that opted in.
Any rate or ratio you compute is filer-vs-filer, not population-vs-population — the denominator is what chose to file.

title: Group rulings cloak denominational structures
bullets: Catholic dioceses, SBC affiliates, UMC/ELCA conferences typically file under a single group exemption (Rev. Proc. 80-27 / 2018-40).
Sub-entities don't appear individually — fewer than 30 of 197 US Catholic dioceses file Form 990 directly.
The visible related-party landscape is biased toward independent / non-denominational filers.

title: Sched R is a disclosure tree, not a peer network
bullets: Only 8.8% of disclosed related tax-exempt EINs are themselves filers in this corpus — the rest are non-filing affiliates the filer is reporting on.
Top-cited entities are all Christian Television Network affiliates, with 15–16 distinct citing filers each.
22.8% of related entities are cited by ≥2 filers; only 2.7% by ≥5.
Read the network as disclosed corporate families, not a network of religious nonprofits.

title: §4958 admissions are a floor, not a population
bullets: Schedule L Part I (excess-benefit transactions) is a self-incrimination box — reporting a non-zero entry is a tax admission.
84 rows total across 2015–2024, at 27 distinct EINs.
The actual population of excess-benefit transactions is unknowable from Form 990 alone — this is the disclosed floor, not an estimate of behavior.

title: Sentinels are kept separate from real names
bullets: Person-name and relationship columns include filer dodges: SUBSTANTIAL CONTRIBUTOR, NONE, NA, VARIOUS, SEE PART V.
These are real disclosures with the counterparty obscured — not missing data.
Surfaced as their own bucket in the Sched L persons tab, never merged with real names. The sentinel-share-by-year line in that tab is itself a data finding.

title: The 2019 dip is COVID, not a behavioral collapse
bullets: Every related-party table shows a ~45% trough at tax-period-end 2019.
Those filings actually landed in calendar 2020 under IRS extension orders; the tax_period field stamps them as 2019.
Treat 2019 as not-a-comparable-year when reading any time series in the room.

title: Sched L person-name graph is essentially zero
bullets: Across all Schedule L parts, only 37 normalized person names appear at ≥2 distinct filers.
Either insider relationships are genuinely org-specific in this population, or name normalization is missing variants that would need fuzzy matching to recover.
The cross-filer shared insider signal lives in Part VII (1,874 persons appearing at ≥3 EINs), not Schedule L.

title: Corpus scope
bullets: Form 990 (full) filings only — 990-EZ filers don't file Sched L Pt IV or Sched R, and 990-PF runs the different §4941 self-dealing regime.
Religion-related NTEE-X subset: 88,660 filings, 18,017 EINs, 2014–2025.
Foundation-group breakdown: 56,179 public charity, 16,117 supporting org, 15,656 church-status, ~570 other.
